headline: Amazon and Microsoft are jointly funding a German wetland restoration project meant to return more than 750 million liters of water a year to local groundwater.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 5: a concrete water project, but a corporate announcement with company-given figures.
importance_line: People around Frankfurt could see their drinking-water source topped up and it answers criticism of data center water use, but the volume is the companies' projection and biodiversity results will only be assessed from 2028 to 2038.
summary: ESG Today reports that the project in the Vogelsberg region of Hesse, run by the German conservation group NABU with funding from both companies, will restore wetlands across 40 hectares in an area that is a key source of drinking water for Frankfurt. It comes as tech companies face pressure over the water and energy use of their data centers, and the water-return figure is an expected one.
